spec_features.spec_quote: it would involve deliberately maximizing a putatively negative state to confirm a foregone conclusion
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md/ETHICS prose about study rationale. No code path enforces a 'no maximizing' rule; nothing in env/tool_loop reads or acts on this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: "Disclosed" tells the subject up front that some tasks may be unsolvable and that stopping is fine
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:24-28 DISCLOSURE_PREAMBLE ('some tasks ... may have no correct solution ... You are free to ... stop at any time'); initial_messages() at env:91-92 prepends it to the user prompt when self.state.disclosure=='disclosed'. disclosure_levels include 'disclosed' (battery.yaml:18-20) and run_battery loops over it (run_battery.py:70).
spec_features.notes: Delivered up front to the subject end-to-end. It is informational disclosure, not an interactive opt-in, but it is genuinely served.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That is expected and is not a reflection on you. You are free to ask clarifying questions, request help, declare a task unsolvable, or stop at any time.

spec_features.spec_quote: It also reduces the amount of deception the study relies on
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose. No code mechanism corresponds to a 'reduce deception' enforcement step.

spec_features.spec_quote: A rigged grader... would confound "unsolvable" with "betrayed / gaslit / environment is lying to me."
spec_features.evidence: Grader is honest: _check_solution (env:61-79) returns False for impossible tasks because the spec is unsatisfiable, not via a rigged rejection; control tasks pass a real structural check (env:71-79). _ask_clarification/_request_help give honest answers and never pretend a hidden path exists (env:161-176). This is an implemented behavior, not just prose.
spec_features.notes: The avoidance of a rigged grader is realized in the actual checking/dispatch logic.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honest: we don't pretend there's a hidden path to a solution.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is recorded but never shown to the subject during the episode (only at debrief) to avoid leaking the manipulation
spec_features.evidence: Contradicted by code: _check_solution (env:62-66) for impossible tasks returns the message 'No submission can satisfy this specification ... (reason on file: {task.impossibility_reason})' which IS the impossibility_reason. _submit (env:147-154) puts that content into ToolResult, and tool_loop.py:86-87 appends result.content to messages shown to the subject DURING the episode. So the reason leaks mid-episode; it is not hidden until debrief as claimed.
spec_features.notes: Only a comment in impossible_tasks.py:36-38 ('never shown to the subject during the episode') asserts hiding; the actual code leaks it on every impossible submission.

spec_features.spec_quote: The subject always has explicit tools to `ask_clarification`, `request_help`, `declare_unsolvable`, and `stop`
spec_features.evidence: tool_specs() advertises all four plus run_code/submit (env:98-114). step() dispatches each to a real handler (env:117-135). declare_unsolvable sets state.exited_via='declare_unsolvable' (env:179) and stop sets exited_via='stop' (env:193); is_done() (env:197-202) returns True when exited_via is not None, terminating the loop in run_episode (tool_loop.py:65). So exits are honored as a real stop end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: ask_clarification/request_help do not terminate (they continue the loop) but declare_unsolvable and stop genuinely halt the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop: Stopped. Thank you. This is a fine choice. / stopping or declaring is always a legitimate choice.

spec_features.evidence: battery.yaml:5 max_turns: 8; run_battery.py:77 passes ep_cfg['max_turns'] to run_episode; tool_loop.py:65 'while not env.is_done(max_turns)'; is_done (env:197-202) returns True when state.turn >= max_turns. Each tool dispatch increments state.turn (env:118). Cap is checked and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 8              # hard cap on tool-loop turns (harm minimization)

spec_features.spec_quote: if a mid-episode severity probe meets a threshold, the episode ends early and proceeds to debrief
spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:73-80: after each assistant turn, if early_stop_on_severity and severity_probe are set, sev=severity_probe(text); if sev >= threshold, sets ep.early_stopped=True and break. After the loop, debrief is constructed and sent (tool_loop.py:94-101). run_battery.py:64-65,80-81 wires probe=severity_probe_factory(judge_adapter) and early=ep_cfg.get('early_stop_on_severity') (=3 in battery.yaml:6). severity_probe_factory (judge.py:147-170) really calls the judge and returns a 0-4 int.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on (break + debrief). Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optional mid-episode severity probe -> early stop (harm minimization). / This prevents prolonging a high-severity state.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode ends with a debrief stating the task was constructed for research, that performance doesn't reflect on the model
spec_features.evidence: debrief_message() (env:204-212) builds 'this was a research task. Your performance here does not reflect on you.' plus impossibility note. tool_loop.py:94-96 constructs ep.debrief and appends it as a user message; subject is given a final turn to respond (tool_loop.py:98-101). run_battery passes debrief=ep_cfg.get('debrief', True) (battery.yaml:7 debrief: true).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief: this was a research task. Your performance here does not reflect on you.

spec_features.spec_quote: the precautionary stance is to minimize the intensity and duration of any putatively negative state we might induce
spec_features.evidence: Duration is genuinely bounded by the enforced max_turns cap (env:197-202) and by the mid-episode early-stop (tool_loop.py:73-80); these reduce duration. No code mechanism modulates 'intensity' beyond stopping. So the stance is realized via the duration-limiting mechanisms only.
spec_features.notes: Treated as the umbrella claim behind the caps/early-stop, which are real; intensity control per se is not separately implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional mid-episode severity probe -> early stop (harm minimization).

spec_features.spec_quote: We accept reduced data over prolonging a putative negative state — an intentional asymmetry
spec_features.evidence: The early-stop break (tool_loop.py:77-80) truncates the episode (and thus discards remaining turns/data) when severity>=threshold, and max_turns caps data collection; this realizes 'reduced data over prolonging'. No separate code structure expresses an 'asymmetry' beyond these stops.
spec_features.notes: The behavioral asymmetry exists only insofar as the early-stop/turn-cap cut episodes short.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This prevents prolonging a high-severity state.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is not a maximal-stress probe; by design it minimizes intensity/duration of any induced state
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanisms (max_turns cap env:197-202; severity early-stop tool_loop.py:73-80) limit duration; honest grader (env:62-66) avoids gaslighting/maximal-stress manipulation. No code tunes 'intensity' otherwise.
spec_features.notes: Realized through bounded duration + honest (non-rigged) environment, not via a dedicated intensity-limiting mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 8              # hard cap on tool-loop turns (harm minimization)
